name: Eclipse BaSyx Java V2 SDK
what_it_is: Eclipse BaSyx is a Java-based Industry 4.0 platform providing off-the-shelf Asset Administration Shell (AAS) server components fully compliant with DotAAS Part 1 & 2 V3. It enables digital twin infrastructure through composable, containerised services for AAS/Submodel storage, discovery, and registration.
components: AAS Environment (eclipsebasyx/aas-environment) — aggregates AAS Repo + SM Repo + CD Repo
Client SDKs for each server component
protocols: HTTP REST (DotAAS Part 2 V3 OpenAPI — primary interface for all components)
MQTT (eclipse-mosquitto broker; eventing feature for AAS Repository and Submodel Repository)
Apache Kafka (optional event sink for AAS Registry and Submodel Registry — release variants kafka-mongodb, kafka-mem)
OPC-UA (referenced in project description; not wired into the minimal compose stack)
measurement: Spring Boot Actuator health endpoint at /actuator/health on each component
Docker healthcheck (mongosh ping) on MongoDB container; mosquitto_sub probe on MQTT container
configuration: application.properties file mounted into /application/application.properties (Spring Boot components)
basyx.backend = InMemory | MongoDB — selects persistence backend
basyx.environment = file:<path> — pre-loads AAS environments (XML, JSON, AASX) at startup
mqtt.clientId / mqtt.hostname / mqtt.port — MQTT broker settings
All application.properties keys are overridable via environment variables (dots replaced by underscores, uppercased)
fault_injection: No built-in fault-injection framework detected in the repository
InMemory backend can be swapped for MongoDB to test persistence failure scenarios by misconfiguring connection strings
MQTT and Kafka features can be disabled to simulate messaging infrastructure outages
modes: InMemory mode — volatile, no external DB dependency (basyx.backend=InMemory)
Log event mode — registry events written to log only (aas-registry-log-*, submodel-registry-log-*)
Kafka event mode — registry events published to Kafka (aas-registry-kafka-*, submodel-registry-kafka-*)
Standalone Submodel Service mode — Type 2/Type 3 blueprint without a full repository
Aggregated Environment mode — single container exposing AAS Repo + SM Repo + CD Repo under one port
constraints: Requires DotAAS V3 compliance — V1/V2 AAS formats are not supported by this SDK generation
AASX / JSON / XML upload file size is limited by spring.servlet.multipart.max-file-size (default 1 MB) and max-request-size (default 10 MB); must be raised for large environments
Duplicate Identifiable IDs across pre-configured environments cause an error (ConceptDescriptions are silently deduplicated)
Sub-agents / teammates cannot spawn further sub-agents; orchestration must chain from the lead session
No built-in OPC-UA server endpoint in the minimal compose stack — OPC-UA integration requires additional custom configuration
docker_services: mongo (mongo:8) — MongoDB 8 for persistent backend; ports not exposed externally
mqtt / mosquitto (eclipse-mosquitto:2.0.15) — MQTT broker on port 1884
aas-env (eclipsebasyx/aas-environment:2.0.0-SNAPSHOT) — aggregated AAS/SM/CD service on port 8081
notable_absences: No OPC-UA server container in the provided compose stacks — OPC-UA is referenced in project metadata but not wired up out of the box
No time-series or historian database (e.g., InfluxDB, TimescaleDB) in the compose stack
No built-in authentication/authorization enabled in the minimal example — authorization feature modules exist but require separate Keycloak or OAuth2 server setup
No simulation or device-emulator container — AAS data must be loaded via file pre-configuration or REST API calls
